articles.title: A Tiny Robot That Swims With Living Muscles
articles.summary: MIT scientists built a gum-sized swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that contract when light shines on them. The tiny biohybrid robot steered through an underwater maze and may one day explore fragile places too delicate for ordinary machines.

articles.title: Halley's Comet Leaves a Trail of Shooting Stars
articles.summary: Earth is passing through debris left by Halley's Comet, creating the Orionid meteor shower. A photographer in Georgia captured three bright meteors near Orion, and the shower remains active until Nov. 7.

articles.title: A $10 Chip That Could Put a Lab on Your Wrist
articles.summary: Cambridge researchers built a $10 spectrometer chip with laboratory-level precision. In tests it identified materials perfectly and measured blood glucose without needles, though more testing is needed before real medical use.
